title: Devolution and benefits—five lessons for Andy Burnham
gist: Patrick and Brewer argue that before Andy Burnham's government devolves business-rate revenue to English mayors, it must learn from the UK's already-fragmented, poorly understood devolution of social security. Drawing on the Nuffield-funded 'Safety Nets' study, they set out five lessons, including that Council Tax Reduction shows the harm of localising settled rules and that devolved revenue must match devolved responsibilities.

insights.claim: Chancellor John Healey's budget made devolving business-rate income generation to mayoral authorities the centrepiece of what he called 'the most radical act of devolution in a generation', with new devolution deals planned across 10 areas in England.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift in UK local fiscal arrangements that will affect local authority finances and regional investment.
insights.quote: The centrepiece of this is the devolution to mayoral authorities of income generation from business rates, with connected plans to create new devolution deals across 10 areas in England.
insights.locator: Rewiring the state through increased English

insights.claim: The authors characterise the UK budget as fiscally conservative and gradualist overall, making its devolution plans comparatively radical, with detail deferred to a White Paper this autumn and a 'fiscal devolution roadmap'.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Fiscal policy is cautious overall; the main structural risk/opportunity lies in how devolution is implemented.
insights.locator: Rewiring the state through increased English

insights.claim: Andy Burnham, as prime minister, has made rewiring the state through English devolution front and centre of his political project.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Devolution is a core governing priority, so related legislation is likely to proceed.
insights.locator: Rewiring the state through increased English

themes.theme: UK social security is already devolved

insights.claim: UK social security is far less centralised and uniform than people or political rhetoric assume: Scotland runs its own social security agency and payments such as the Scottish Child Payment, and Northern Ireland mitigates the Benefit Cap and Bedroom Tax.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Welfare policy outcomes and spending already vary by nation, complicating UK-wide forecasts of benefit spending.
insights.quote: Social security is far less centralised and uniform than people think, or than political rhetoric so often implies.

insights.claim: Locally controlled social security support across the UK has grown from almost nothing in 2010-11 but accounted for just 1.2 per cent of total UK government social security spending in 2024-25.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Local welfare remains a tiny share of spending, so devolution's fiscal footprint in welfare is small so far.

insights.claim: Wales has fewer formal social security powers but its new Plaid Cymru government wants more, and it already uses a novel discretionary support model involving a private contractor, a local authority and a voluntary organisation.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Pressure for further welfare devolution to Wales is likely under the new government.

insights.claim: The authors argue the devolved nations are the UK's longest-running experiments in exactly the trade-offs Burnham faces in devolving to English mayors.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Outcomes in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are leading indicators for English devolution.

themes.theme: Free school meals as postcode lottery

insights.claim: Free school meal provision differs across every part of the UK: Wales covers all state primary pupils, Scotland covers up to Primary 5, London's mayor funds universal provision for years three to six, England covers all Universal Credit households, and Northern Ireland has no universal provision and a tighter means test.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Illustrates how devolution creates divergent public spending commitments by region.

insights.claim: When parents from all four nations learned how free school meal provision differed, almost all were angry, including those not losing out, illustrating that tailored local support is experienced by others as a postcode lottery.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Visible regional disparities can create political pressure to level up provision, raising spending.
insights.quote: How that hasn’t caused an outcry, I don’t know

insights.claim: UK ministers discussing child poverty or youth worklessness often show little understanding of how far social security devolution already reaches, partly because no institutions encourage learning between nations.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Policy designed from Whitehall may misfire because it ignores devolved variation.

insights.claim: Devolution's promise of 'policy laboratories' has not been realised in social security: the DWP shows little sign of learning from Scotland's Adult Disability Payment ahead of the Timms Review of Personal Independence Payments.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: The Timms Review outcome on PIP is a key upcoming welfare spending decision; Scotland's model is an untapped template.

themes.theme: What should and shouldn't be localised

insights.claim: Since 2013, every English council has had to design its own Council Tax Reduction means test, leading to legal challenges, the return of cliff-edges Universal Credit was meant to remove, and the least generous schemes concentrated in more deprived areas.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: A cautionary case of localisation worsening outcomes, relevant to evaluating new English devolution deals.
insights.quote: But Council Tax Reduction shows what happens when the wrong thing is localised.

insights.claim: The authors' rule of thumb: localise where local knowledge improves decisions, such as discretionary crisis support, and keep national anything where rules are settled and consistency matters, including basic income adequacy.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Provides a framework for judging which devolved powers are likely to succeed.
insights.quote: So localise where local knowledge improves decisions, and keep national anything where the rules are settled and consistency matters, including the basic adequacy of incomes.

insights.claim: Devolved revenue must match devolved responsibilities both in scale and in how both move with the economic cycle; otherwise local leaders are blamed for gaps they didn't create.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Business-rate devolution exposes local finances to cyclical revenue swings against counter-cyclical welfare demand.

insights.claim: In the 2010s devolution was used as a stealthy way to cut the welfare state via Council Tax Reduction and crisis support, a practice some call 'austerity dumping'.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Risk that new devolution deals become a channel for hidden spending cuts, eroding trust in local government.

insights.claim: The authors predict-recommend that the forthcoming devolution White Paper must state principles for which domains are devolved, commit to properly funding devolved powers, and create mechanisms for governments to learn from one another.
insights.speaker: Ruth Patrick, Mike Brewer
insights.so_what: Watch the White Paper for funding commitments and intergovernmental mechanisms as signals of devolution quality.
